signal.description: Electrical timing of a trigger, gate, marker, clock, reference or sync connection. Hardware performs the timing; the description records it.

device.description: Device whose operation is called (a Basic Operation). Omit it to use a saved Standard or Workflow Operation named by operation.

repeat.description: Run the step this many times in turn, at each point of its sweep if it has one; what it returns is gathered over a last axis named repeat

retake.description: With sweep or repeat on a device operation, in a step graph: points a lost condition put in doubt are taken again, with the arguments they were given, once a pass restored the condition and before the next operation; what the sweep gathers holds what the retakes read. Not with adapt

conditions.description: What must hold on the platform for its experiments. The Runtime verifies each condition, corrects it when it drifted and trusts an accepted verification for valid_for.

kind.description: Optional, extensible category. Dependencies are defined only by after.

after.description: Conditions of this platform that must hold first.

samples.description: Readings one verification takes; a tolerance judges their statistic.

usable.description: When not met, the measurement itself means nothing and the conditions in after are verified.

reference.description: Values of the accepted verification kept with experiments that rely on the condition.

correct.description: What restores the condition, tried in order; each is followed by a verification. An operation, or tune.

settle.description: Seconds between a correction and its verification.

valid_for.description: Seconds an accepted verification is trusted.

upkeep.description: Declared, the Runtime keeps the platform's conditions: while the instruments a pass needs are idle, it starts a pass for conditions that are unknown, due, lost, about to expire or forecast to leave their tolerance. Each automatic pass is recorded with automatic: true and its reasons, and never runs a step that asks a person.

conditions.description: Conditions to keep; default all of the platform's and its instruments'.

ahead_s.description: Observe this long before validity ends or the drift forecast reaches the tolerance.

retry_s.description: Wait before another attempt at a condition the last attempt did not bring to hold.

correct.description: false: observe and record only; nothing is corrected.

disturbances.description: Events a person reports at the platform, such as an opened enclosure, a reconnected fiber or a changed sample, each with the conditions it acts on. Reporting one makes those conditions and what depends on them due, with the event as the reason.

description.description: What happens and how it acts on the apparatus.

conditions.description: Conditions of this platform or its instruments the event acts on directly; what depends on them follows.

conditionStep.description: One operation: a device operation, or a saved operation without device.

value.description: Path into the verification result; default ["value"].

minimum.description: A number in the unit of the reading, or a quantity with its unit such as "20 mK" when the reading's unit is described.

maximum.description: A number in the unit of the reading, or a quantity with its unit such as "20 mK" when the reading's unit is described.

statistic.description: With samples: judge the mean (default), the standard deviation, the span or the slope per second of the readings.

oneOf.description: A quantity with its unit, such as "-253.15 °C"

target.description: A nominal or certified value, or the reading that gives it, such as the setpoint the instrument holds. The value judged is the deviation from it.

within.description: With target: the absolute tolerance of the deviation.

relative.description: With target: the tolerance as a fraction of the target; added to within.

conditionTuning.description: A correction the Runtime performs itself: it adjusts the settings one at a time against the verification value, steps back from a setting that does not improve it, and halves the step when no move helps.

tune.description: One setting, or several adjusted jointly.

goal.description: Default: maximize with only a minimum in accept, minimize with only a maximum, center with both.

until.description: accept stops once the tolerance is met.

gain.description: Smallest improvement that counts, above the noise of the verification.

operation.description: The operation that sets the value.

arguments.description: Other, fixed arguments of that operation.

read.description: The operation that returns the present setting.

resolution.description: Smallest step worth taking; default step / 16.

source.description: A value an earlier step returned: path selects inside its result or, with view, inside a view of an array it returned

view.description: Read the value from a view of an array the step returned: field, along, at, start, stop, low, high, points, peak; path then selects inside the view. Along two axes, a map, along names both and the others give one value per axis. peak max, or min for a dip, finds the line: path ["peak", "center"] or ["peak", "width"]; level finds where the trace crosses a value: path ["crossings", 0, "at"]; fit line gives the straight line through it: path ["fit", "slope"] or ["fit", "zero"]; fit lorentzian or gaussian a line of that shape: path ["fit", "center"] or ["fit", "width"]. With one other axis not fixed, these are read at each of its positions: path ["rows", "peak", 0, "center"] (see docs/runtime/drivers.md, Reading arrays)

prominence.description: With peak, read every line that stands out by this much: path ["peaks"]

level.description: Read where the trace crosses this value, between samples, rising or falling

fit.description: Fit a straight line, or a line of Lorentzian or Gaussian shape, through the trace by least squares

sweep.description: Run this step at each value of these parameters, one point after another, the first changing slowest; what it returns is gathered into arrays over the sweep, at most 10000 points. A list gives the values (numbers, or strings as labels); start, stop and points, or center, span and points, give evenly spaced numbers. An end of a range may be read from an earlier step, as a binding is, such as where a coarse sweep found most power; each point then takes its value when it runs. With adapt, each point is placed from what the earlier ones read, closer together where the reading changes most

adapt.description: Place each point from what the earlier ones read: the path to the number each point reads, such as ["power"]; points come closer where it changes most (one swept parameter, 2 to 1000 points, gathered in order of value)

Place each point from what the earlier ones read: the path to the number each point reads, such as ["power"]; points come closer where it changes most (one swept parameter, 2 to 1000 points, gathered in order of value)

until.description: Stop a sweep or repetition after a point whose reading is above or below a limit, or is not a number, or once a view of what it has gathered is: the later points are skipped without reaching an instrument, and the steps after the sweep run. The first point always runs

path.description: The number each point reads, in what its operation returns or in the named result of its use, such as ["current"]; with view, the number in that view, such as ["summary", "error"]

above.description: Stop after a point that reads more than this

below.description: Stop after a point that reads less than this; with above, the sweep goes on while the reading stays between them

view.description: Read path in this view of what the sweep has gathered so far, before each point, such as {"field": "power"}, or {"field": "s21", "fit": "lorentzian"} with path ["fit", "errors", "center"]; while it gives no number, the sweep goes on. Such a sweep has at most 1000 points

points.description: How many points run before until is read, so that an error from a few points does not stop the sweep

retry.description: When the instrument call fails, make it again after after_s seconds, up to times more times; each failed attempt stays in the operation record under attempts, and what it wrote is discarded. A call whose outcome is unknown, a refusal before the call and a cancellation are not made again. For operations safe to repeat, such as a reading or a move to a position

times.description: How many more times the call may be made

after_s.description: Seconds to wait before each further call

seek.description: Find where a reading is largest or smallest: each point moves the parameters over by a compass search from start, keeping a move whose reading improves on the best by more than gain, trying the other direction when one does not help, and halving every step when none does; the search ends once each step is below its resolution, and the later points are skipped. What it gathered holds the readings over an axis named evaluation, the places read under positions, and the best under best (index, at, reading). Not with sweep, repeat, until or retake

maximize.description: The path to the number each point reads that the seek makes largest, such as ["power"]

minimize.description: The path to the number each point reads that the seek makes smallest

over.description: Each parameter the seek moves, up to 10, with the range it never leaves

minimum.description: The lowest value the seek takes; a number, or read from an earlier step as a binding is

maximum.description: The highest value the seek takes

step.description: The first move, halved each time no move helps

start.description: Where the seek starts; the middle of the range by default. May be read from an earlier step, such as where a coarse sweep read most

resolution.description: The smallest step worth taking; a sixteenth of step by default

points.description: How many places the seek may read

gain.description: The smallest improvement that counts, above the noise of a reading

targetReading.description: The reading that gives a target: one operation and the path to the number in its result.
